record.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in Visibility Graphs of Points, Segments and Polygons
record.context_brief: Crossing numbers of bar k-visibility graphs
record.original_question: What is the largest possible crossing number of a bar k-visibility graph?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 25 The crossing number of a graph is the minimum possible number of crossings with which the graph can be drawn in the plane. What is the largest crossing number of a bar k-visibility graph?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A bar representation is a finite collection of pairwise disjoint horizontal closed line segments ("bars") in the plane, no two having the same y-coordinate. For a fixed nonnegative integer k, the bar k-visibility graph of such a representation is the graph whose vertices are the bars, and in which two distinct bars b and b' are joined by an edge if and only if there exists a vertical (closed) line segment connecting a point of b to a point of b' that meets the interiors of at most k other bars.

The crossing number cr(G) of a graph G is the minimum, over all drawings of G in the plane with vertices as distinct points and edges as continuous curves joining their endpoints, of the number of pairs of edges that cross.

Determine, as a function of the number of vertices n (and the parameter k), the maximum value of cr(G) over all bar k-visibility graphs G on n vertices. In particular, give a tight asymptotic (or exact) bound on the largest possible crossing number of a bar k-visibility graph.
artifact.status_search_result: Search results return work on bar k-visibility graphs concerning edge counts, chromatic number, thickness, and the largest complete bar k-visibility graph (e.g., K_8 for k=1, conjecturally K_{4k+4}), but no source explicitly resolves the maximum crossing number of bar k-visibility graphs. The status of this specific question therefore appears unresolved in the located literature.

status_evidence.title: Bar k-Visibility Graphs: Bounds on the Number of Edges, Chromatic Number, and Thickness
status_evidence.snippet: Bounds on edges, chromatic number, and thickness of bar k-visibility graphs are established; crossing number is not addressed.
status_evidence.claim: Known bounds focus on edges, chromatic number, thickness, not on crossing number.

status_evidence.title: Further Results on Bar k-Visibility Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Sharp upper bounds on the maximum number of edges and the largest complete bar k-visibility graph are established.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work treats edge bounds and complete subgraphs; crossing number question is not resolved here.
